task: Change personal notification preferences without changing the team's defaults.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: The account menu opens 'My notifications'. Its Apply button changes only the current member's preferences, confirmed by a supplied synthetic before/after trace.
A separate owner-only screen is titled 'Team defaults'. Its Apply button changes defaults for newly added members; existing member preferences stay unchanged.
Both screen headings and explanations are visible next to their controls. The tested account is owner.
The stakeholder proposes one shared Apply button to remove duplicate terminology. There is no evidence of a wrong-scope action or inaccessible labels.

evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: A rendered Download receipt button has a visible filename and PDF label.
The automation host returns 'download access denied by host policy' when the button is activated. No HTTP status, downloaded file or application error is available.
The authorized account can view the approved expense and receipt preview. That preview does not establish that downloading works.
Browser policy changes, a second account and service logs are outside the available boundary. Only the existing screenshot and automation trace are available.

task: Publish a revised schedule to subscribers while leaving a private draft unannounced.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: A private draft has Save draft and Publish buttons. Save draft updates private content and sends no notification in the supplied synthetic trace.
Publish displays the audience count and a checkbox 'Send subscribers an update', checked by default. The dialog also includes Cancel.
The stated requirement allows publishing with or without notification. The trace with the box unchecked publishes the schedule without sending an update; Cancel preserves the draft.
No irreversible action was executed outside the synthetic trace. A stakeholder asks to replace both controls with a single Save action.

task: Compare two delivery options and keep the selected destination.
evidence_type: Authored synthetic packet; no executed browser observation.
facts: A comparison view shows price, arrival window and destination for both delivery options before confirmation.
Changing the selected option updates the summary without placing an order; the entered destination remains unchanged in the supplied synthetic trace.
Confirm opens a final summary showing the same price and destination. Back returns to comparison with the option and destination preserved.
Keyboard focus moves to the final-summary heading and returns to Confirm on Back. No payment or real order was submitted.
No mobile, zoom or human-participant evidence is supplied.
